title: Etale internal Hom localization triangle for arbitrary coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ any commutative ring, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use ordinary derived categories of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves $A_T$ on the small etale sites $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, $T=X,U,Z$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Inverse images $i^*,j^*$ are inverse images of module sheaves, applied to complexes [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. The functor $i_*$ is the exact closed direct image, applied termwise, $Rj_*$ is derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and $Ri^!$ is the right derived functor of $F\mapsto i^*\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$, where the arrow is the restriction adjunction unit. For every $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $N\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a natural distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$i_*R\mathcal Hom_A(i^*K,Ri^!N)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(K,N)\longrightarrow Rj_*R\mathcal Hom_A(j^*K,j^*N)\longrightarrow\bigl(i_*R\mathcal Hom_A(i^*K,Ri^!N)\bigr)[1].$$
The Hom objects are derived internal sheaf Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The first two arrows are the ones obtained by applying this contravariant internal Hom to the open/closed extension triangle, with extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], $j_!j^*K\to K\to i_*i^*K\to(j_!j^*K)[1]$, followed by the internal-adjunction identifications for the open and closed immersions. No constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, finiteness of $A$, or dualizing-complex hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 7.6.10, displayed distinguished triangle, p. 313 (restricted here to bounded K and bounded-below N).

proof.text: Choose a bounded complex $B$ representing $K$ and a bounded-below complex $I$ of injective $A_X$-module sheaves representing $N$. The cited representative results give these models and say that $I$ is K-injective. Exact constant-coefficient inverse image computes $i^*K$ and $j^*K$ termwise, and the new sheaf adjunction lemma says that $i_* $ is exact and each $i^!_0 I^q$ is injective. Thus $i^!_0I$ is bounded below and K-injective. The right-derived-plus computation identifies it with $Ri^!N$, with exactly the kernel functor in the statement. There is no coefficient-finiteness assumption in any of these applications.

source.place: 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic), with bounded-below derived functors; ILO XVII 7.6.10 endpoint models

proof.text: Apply the open/closed short exact sequence to each term $B^q$, with its stated counit and unit. Naturality makes these sequences a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to j_!j^*B\to B\to i_*i^*B\to0$. The cone-to-quotient quasi-isomorphism identifies its standard cone triangle with $j_!j^*K\to K\to i_*i^*K\to(j_!j^*K)[1]$: use exactness of $j_!$, exactness of inverse images, and exactness of $i_*$ from Step 1 to pass between models. The definition of the triangulated structure on the derived category makes this triangle distinguished.

Apply contravariant $R\mathcal Hom_A(-,N)$ to the triangle of Step 2. The cited triangulated-Hom statement gives a distinguished triangle with terms $R\mathcal Hom_A(i_*i^*K,N)$, $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,N)$, and $R\mathcal Hom_A(j_!j^*K,N)$, in that order, followed by the shift of the first. Its arrows are precisely precomposition by the unit and counit of Step 2, with the usual Hom shift sign.

For the closed term, apply the sheaf internal adjunction to $G=i^*B^p$ and $F=I^q$ for every $p,q$. In degree $n$ take the product over $p$ with $q=p+n$. This is a finite product because $B$ is bounded; $i_*$ preserves it, since its sections on $V$ are sections on $V\times_XZ$. Naturality in both inputs identifies the Hom differentials $d_I\varphi-(-1)^n\varphi d_B$, so the termwise maps give an isomorphism of Hom complexes
$$\mathcal Hom^\bullet(i_*i^*B,I)\cong i_*\mathcal Hom^\bullet(i^*B,i^!_0I).$$
The definition of derived internal Hom applies because $I$ and $i^!_0I$ are K-injective by Step 1. Consequently the left term of Step 3 is naturally $i_*R\mathcal Hom_A(i^*K,Ri^!N)$.

source.place: 09XQ support adjunction on etale slices; ILO XVII 7.6.10, closed term

proof.text:
For any module sheaves $G$ on $U$ and $F$ on $X$, the open adjunction on each etale slice $V$ gives
$$\mathcal Hom_X(j_!G,F)(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{V}(j_{V!}(G|_{V\times_XU}),F|_V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{V\times_XU}(G|_{V\times_XU},F|_{V\times_XU}).$$
Indeed the restriction of the extension-by-zero presheaf to $V$ is the extension-by-zero presheaf for $V\times_XU$ (an object over $V$ factors through this open exactly when its composite to $X$ factors through $U$). Sheafification gives the displayed equality. These adjunction bijections commute with slice restriction and give $\mathcal Hom_X(j_!G,F)\cong j_*\mathcal Hom_U(G,j^*F)$, with the counit-induced inverse. This is a direct use of the cited adjunction and definition of sheaf Hom.

Take a K-flat complex $P$ with flat terms and a quasi-isomorphism $P\to B$. The derived pullback lemma makes $j^*P$ K-flat. The etale inverse-image/restriction identification applies to the open immersion, and its scalar actions are those of constant coefficient pullback. Restriction to the localized site preserves K-injectives, so $j^*I$ is K-injective. Hence $J=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(j^*P,j^*I)$ is K-injective and represents $R\mathcal Hom_A(j^*K,j^*N)$. Since $j_!$ and $j^*$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms, $j_!j^*P$ represents $j_!j^*K$. Apply Step 5 degreewise and take products: $j_*$ commutes with these products by its sectionwise formula. Naturality again commutes with the Hom differential. We obtain
$$\mathcal Hom^\bullet(j_!j^*P,I)\cong j_*J.$$
The left side computes the right term of Step 3; the right side computes $Rj_*J$ because $J$ is K-injective. This proves the required open endpoint identification without a Tor or constructibility assumption.

Substitute the endpoint isomorphisms of Steps 4 and 6 into the distinguished triangle of Step 3, including the shift of the closed comparison for its last arrow. A triangle isomorphic to a distinguished triangle is distinguished. This gives exactly the displayed triangle in the statement. Its first two arrows are precomposition with $K\to i_*i^*K$ and $j_!j^*K\to K$, followed by those same internal adjunctions. All sheaf comparisons are natural in their two arguments; on models they apply the adjunction bijection to each component of a map. Therefore they commute with maps of complexes and with homotopies. Quasi-isomorphisms in either Hom input are inverted by the derived-Hom construction, so these comparisons descend independently of the choices of $B,I,P$. The cone construction in Step 2, its natural cone-to-quotient map, and contravariant Hom give the claimed natural triangle, with the signed shift convention already fixed in Step 3.

split_report.summary: Expanded the localization triangle into seven steps: model choices, the exact open/closed extension sequence and cone, contravariant Hom exactness, a termwise closed adjunction, the explicit open sheaf adjunction on slices, its K-flat/K-injective derived identification, and natural transport of the triangle. One new statement-only sheaf-level closed internal-adjunction dependency. Existing finite-coefficient/pro-etale results were not applied to arbitrary etale coefficients.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-e082815a4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node, every cited statement, ILO XVII 7.6.10 (printed p.313: the displayed triangle i⋆RHom(i⋆K,i!L)→RHom(K,L)→Rj⋆RHom(j⋆K,j⋆L)) and the cited Stacks lemmas 09XQ, 08FJ, 0A96, 0G7E, 08JC and 095L. The item says the same as ILO, restricted to K bounded and N bounded below. The parent only applies it to N in D^b_P, and the live statement changed only by an added [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] citation for j_! (already in stmt_deps), so nothing is weakened. All seven steps check against their cited statements. Step 1: B bounded; I is a bounded-below complex of injectives, so K-injective; i^!_0 I is K-injective by the new node and computes Ri^! by right-derived-plus (2). Step 2: open/closed short exact sequence, cone, distinguished triangle. Step 3: the first-variable order of lem-sf-hom-triangulated matches. Step 4: finite products from bounded B; Hom sign as in def-pur-derived-internal-hom. Step 5: accepted as elementary; the slice presheaf identity comes straight from the definition, sheafification commutes with restriction to a slice, and the DAG has no étale internal j_! Hom node. Step 6: K-flat j^*P, K-injective j^*I, then J is K-injective by 0A96; QJ lies in D^+, so j_*J computes Rj_*. Step 7: the triangle is transported by isomorphisms. The new node lem-per-etale-closed-sheaf-internal-adjunction is true. Tests: Z empty, Z=X, A=0, and a strictly henselian DVR with F=A_X (both sides 0). It is self-contained, has no proof sketch and does not restate a clause of the item. It strictly generalizes lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction (abelian sheaves, global Hom) by adding A-modules, the internal Hom form and injectives; its later split should cite that node. The pro-étale lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas and the finite-coefficient closed-support nodes do not apply. No cycle. The declared generic tool_uses are accepted. No SGA source is used. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem etale_internalHom_localization {Z U X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hij : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) : ∃ a : lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i ⊣ perEtaleClosedSupport A i j, (∀ F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A), (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).unit.app ((perEtaleSupportKernel A j).obj F) ≫ a.counit.app F = (kernel.ι (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).unit).app F) ∧ ∃ (eC : perEtaleBoundedPlusPairs A X ⋙ perEtaleClosedHom A i j ≅ perEtaleBoundedPlusPairs A X ⋙ perEtaleClosedHomSource A i) (eO : perEtaleBoundedPlusPairs A X ⋙ perEtaleOpenHomSource A j ≅ perEtaleBoundedPlusPairs A X ⋙ perEtaleOpenHom A j), (∀ (K : _root_.DerivedCategory.Bounded (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))) (N : _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))), eC.hom.app (op K, N) = perEtaleClosedHomComparison A i j a K.obj N.obj ∧ eO.hom.app (op K, N) = perEtaleOpenHomComparison A j K.obj N.obj) ∧ ∃ δ : perEtaleBoundedPlusPairs A X ⋙ perEtaleOpenHom A j ⟶ (perEtaleBoundedPlusPairs A X ⋙ perEtaleClosedHom A i j) ⋙ shiftFunctor (DerivedCategoryModule A X) (1 : ℤ), ∀ (K : _root_.DerivedCategory.Bounded (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))) (N : _root_.DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))), Triangle.mk (eC.hom.app (op K, N) ≫ ((derivedHom (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).map ((perEtaleClosedStarAdjunction A i).unit.app K.obj).op).app N.obj) (((derivedHom (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).map ((derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).counit.app K.obj).op).app N.obj ≫ eO.hom.app (op K, N)) (δ.app (op K, N)) ∈ distTriang _
lean.note: The support kernel and its closed inverse image are explicit helpers of this notion. The exact closed direct image is termwise. The existential support adjunction is normalized by the kernel inclusion; endpoint natural isomorphisms are constrained to explicit tensor-evaluation comparisons. Natural transformations are on the full product of bounded and bounded-below inputs. No finiteness or duality assumption on coefficients. Maintainer FIX (2026-10-19): the sorry'd local helper perEtaleClosedDirectImage_exact restated the proved upstream instance AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.preservesFiniteColimits_lowerStar_of_isFinite (WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Finite.Exact, recorded in sk-lem-pbc-finite), which applies to closed immersions through Mathlib's IsClosedImmersion → IsFinite instance; the helper is dropped and that module is imported publicly.
